purpose: Sodium is an essential mineral your body needs to work properly. It helps keep your body's fluids balanced, supports nerve function, and helps your muscles — including your heart — contract normally. It may be given as a supplement or IV fluid when your sodium levels are too low, a condition called hyponatremia.
how_it_works: Sodium works by helping control the amount of water in and around your cells. Think of it like a sponge — sodium helps pull and hold water in the right places in your body. When sodium levels are too low, your body's cells can swell with water, which can cause symptoms like confusion, headache, or muscle weakness. Replacing sodium helps restore this balance.
common_side_effects: When taken in appropriate amounts, sodium is generally well tolerated. However, too much sodium can cause fluid retention (swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles), increased blood pressure, thirst, and bloating.
warnings: Too much sodium can be dangerous, especially if you have high blood pressure, heart failure, kidney disease, or liver problems. Correcting very low sodium levels too quickly can cause serious brain complications, so this must always be done carefully under medical supervision. Do not take extra sodium supplements without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Dosing varies widely depending on why you need it and how it is being given. IV sodium is given in a hospital and carefully monitored by your medical team. Oral sodium tablets (like SlowSodium) are sometimes prescribed for chronic low sodium, commonly 600 mg taken 1–3 times daily with meals. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
